column6: Row has three kinds. A literal or template selects the existing version row by its family; a `<name>` placeholder is a capture of this operation's OpenAPI path. column6: If_match is optional, ignored or base-rev. Optional validates and judges the optional header by P/08.0-R006. Ignored does not read it at the creation POSTs or POST batch. If_match is optional, ignored, base-rev or optional-index. Optional validates and judges the optional header by P/08.0-R006. Ignored does not read it at the creation POSTs or POST batch. Base-rev gives If-Match priority and uses base_rev only without that header; if both are present and incompatible, the existing refusal applies (400 refused, field /base_rev); an index next to base_rev is incompatible as in the norm. These rows must include P/08.0-R006 in norm. The ordinary identity, repeat-memory, row-existence and condition order stays P/08.0-R006/R007, including a replay that does not judge the former condition anew.

Optional-index accepts an absent header or a double-quoted store index only; `\"` matches confirmed absence. An unquoted number is 400 `If-Match is a store index`. It requires revision=`-` and absent_revision=`-`; 412 is IndexMoved with field `/index`, current index (`""` for confirmed absence) and optional current row, without a revision counter. Membership PUT returns `{folders,index}` without ETag; an empty list deletes the membership row and returns index `""`. Unknown reads never become absence. Replay is checked before the former condition, as for the other doors.

The review neighbours use the same actual implementation paths. `domain-versioned-edit` also runs role-lines and folder/membership HTTP operations, reads actual store indexes, and retries the same saved request after a committed lost answer; it never synthesizes revision for membership. Folder deletion is verified against the actual tombstone and its ETag.

`domain-role-http` invokes ordinary authenticated role POST/PUT/GET/DELETE and batch handlers, the real spread pass, the real member copy receiver and its local `may`. Fixtures seed valid neutral users/groups/roles, live folders and confirmed member rows. A forbidden legacy role is inserted only to test the ordinary family reader and spread refusal, not to bypass the tested door. Read back actual supervision after creation, omitted-field edit, replacement and clear; exercise unknown/unconfirmed references, self-reference, builtin admin and final-snapshot batch guards. Counters observe actual target writes, not only response codes.

`domain-person-login` invokes the real person login and PBKDF2/signature code. Pause the old request after its confirmed credential read, without a common process lock; through ordinary doors delete the person, advance both clocks beyond the deletion hold and create a new person with the same name and a different password. Resume the old real verification and observe that it produces no token; a fresh ordinary login of the new person succeeds. Output verified iat/exp and flags only, never passwords or JWT bytes.

The two-target-attempt handover fixture uses two real trusted, signed and sealed backups. Suspend actual old restore I/O while the process and its ordinary turn renewals remain live; source call-off/disconnect is not a target completion. Concurrent authorized prepare/take/move must refuse without pending or restore writes. The first claim is made to conflict at its actual store boundary; resume and join old work, then complete a fresh prepare/take of the second copy. Observe the I/O history and actual rows/keys/signer: no old restore write follows the accepted second prepare, and the final state belongs to one copy. No canned claim, crypto verdict, expected state or lock flag replaces these effects.

The cleanup fixture fails an actual obsolete-object delete after a confirmed accepted mark, then issues exact same and nonrefreshing heard requests before a new generation. Count real deletion attempts: the early-return paths neither promise cleanup nor undo the accepted report. The last request reaches cleanup and removes the remainder.

\n**Login time origin (P08 review C5).** When the enabled credential row is confirmed, capture its wall time `credential_at` and a monotonic start before the unlocked PBKDF2 verification. A successful person token uses `iat = credential_at`, `exp = credential_at + TOKEN_LIFETIME`, and response `until = exp`; signing, a later read or a retry cannot refresh this origin. After password verification and immediately before issuance, if the monotonic elapsed duration is at least TOKEN_LIFETIME or wall now is at least exp, return 401 `{error: \refused\", detail: \"login took too long; try again\"}` without a token; a new request rereads its credential and starts anew. A delay after the final time check still cannot extend iat or exp. DELETE and later recreation of the same name therefore cannot turn a suspended verification of the old password into a fresh token for the new person. Ordinary login is unchanged, and keep/kind token issuance is not changed by this login-specific origin.\n"

The same rules apply to `fields.supervision` of a role put in POST `/domain/batch`, over its final snapshot. A missing non-self supervisor role is 400 unknown role; an unreadable referenced role is 503 unavailable. Self-reference is allowed, including creation; it needs no pre-existing self row. All other referenced roles are guarded at their read versions. A request to set or clear supervision on builtin admin is 409 builtin. A stored reference from another role prevents DELETE with 409 role referenced; a self-reference leaves with the role. Reads and writes remain ordinary role operations with the same rights, CAS, counters and repeat memory; no manual store edit is required to enable or remove supervision.\n

column7: Idempotency-Key \u2014 optional repeat memory at all four writing folder/membership operations. If-Match \u2014 ignored by POST creation; ordinary optional revision/index at folder PUT/DELETE, optional-index only at membership PUT (P/08.0 N1.9). A stale condition writes nothing: folders \u2014 412 RevisionMoved, membership \u2014 412 IndexMoved. A replay is judged before the old condition. \n**Target restore exclusion (P08 review C1).** In the target process, authorized `/api/prepare`, `/api/take` and `/domain/move` enter one exclusive restore section after the ordinary identity, turn and request-form checks and before reading/changing pending or starting restore work. An already occupied section returns 503 `{error: \refused\", detail: \"a move is under way here already: seconds, not minutes\"}` without pending/key/state/claim writes. Take holds it through spending pending, opening keys, all restore I/O and the final claim/Entry handling. Prepare holds it through its pending-key write; move holds it through its entire changing operation. A source call-off, HTTP timeout, disconnected caller or cancelled response does not release it while any old handler, submitted I/O or callback can still perform a restore write. Release only after that work has completed or cancellation has been joined so it cannot write; after release the old operation never resumes restore. A new prepare may replace pending before a take starts, as before, but cannot overlap a live take. This local exclusion does not replace the ordinary turn/CAS/unknown-outcome barrier, cryptographic validation, or restore-before-final-claim order.\n"
